name: 52329-shortdecode-qwen306b-1gpu
hardware: 1x H100 80GB HBM3 (one GPU of an a3 node, --gres=gpu:1).
parallelism: TP=1, PP=1, DP=1. One in-process engine, no speculative decoding, no KV connector, no offload tier, no router.
architecture: Qwen3ForCausalLM, bf16, 28 layers, hidden 1024, 16 query heads over 8 KV heads of head_dim 128, vocabulary 151936, ~1.40 GiB in one safetensors shard.
load_profile: concurrent (closed loop), streams=256, warmup 10%, cooldown 10%, 5120 requests bounded, safety_seconds 1800.
workload: Short prompt, long decode, single turn. guidellm `synthetic_text`, 32 prompt tokens and 256 output tokens pinned exactly, `request_format: plain` so no chat template is applied, greedy (`temperature: 0.0`) with `ignore_eos: true`, and every other sampling parameter left at its default. Driven in-process through guidellm's `vllm_python` backend.
purpose: A compact Qwen assistant generating long single-turn completions from brief prompts for 256 concurrent users on one GPU.
launch:
# 52329-shortdecode-qwen306b-1gpu -- the launch config, in `vllm serve --config` form.
# One engine, one H100, a small dense checkpoint under a wide batch of short-prompt /
# long-decode completion traffic. Everything not named here is left at the engine's
# defaults for this device.
#
# VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1 is required for this item and lives in env.yaml.

model: Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B

tensor-parallel-size: 1

# A request in this workload is 32 + 256 = 288 tokens.
max-model-len: 512

# The engine-side admission cap, matched to the client's 256 concurrent streams so they are
# resident together rather than queueing behind a smaller cap.
max-num-seqs: 256

gpu-memory-utilization: 0.90
